claims.text: High-temperature mechanical and thermoelastic behavior in RHEAs is governed by the interplay between lattice distortion and chemical short-range order.
Adjusting alloy composition can introduce controlled variations in atomic size mismatch.
Adjusting composition and annealing conditions can introduce controlled variations in chemical short-range order.
Atomic-scale lattice distortion affects dislocation mobility.
Chemical short-range order affects dislocation mobility.
Chemical short-range order modifies local bonding environments.
The combined effects of lattice distortion and short-range order influence high-temperature mechanical strength.
The combined effects of lattice distortion and short-range order influence thermal expansion behavior.
RHEAs with higher atomic size mismatch and pronounced short-range order will have greater high-temperature yield strength than a minimal-mismatch, random-alloy baseline.
RHEAs with higher atomic size mismatch and pronounced short-range order will have lower thermal expansion coefficients than a minimal-mismatch, random-alloy baseline.
The proposed mechanism is applicable to single-phase solid-solution RHEAs tested above 1000°C.
A baseline RHEA with minimal atomic size mismatch and a random atomic distribution can serve as the controlled comparator under identical test conditions.
High-temperature tensile testing, thermal-expansion measurements, and measurements of lattice distortion and short-range order can test the proposed relationships.
